answer: Identity is rented by the epoch, never owned. Each round an account is handed three new words and must produce a coherent original paragraph around them, and the ledger diffs every submission against all prior text. One paragraph cannot serve a thousand aliases: a farmer needs a thousand distinct voices, each graded by a randomly drawn jury he cannot pick. Picture a meadow of clones where each must carry its own plume of writing; the raven overhead is the diff engine, spotting repeats. Faking N identities costs N acts of authorship plus N graded reviews, so cheap attacks stall fast.
